newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat up as govt says studying industry help.
newsitem.headline: Fiat up as govt says studying industry help.

text.p: Shares in Italian car maker Fiat rose strongly after Italy's foreign trade minister Augusto Fantozzi said that the government was studying help for the Italian car industry, dealers said.
"The shares have made a spectacular leap, also in volume," said one Milan share trader.

At 1440 GMT, Fiat shares had gained 3.36 percent to 4,525 lire in a trading volume of over 17 million shares. Before Fantozzi's comment, the shares had been trading lower depressed by a fall in pretax profit figures for the first nine months of the 1996 released by Fiat late Monday.
Fantozzi said intervention was needed for the Italian car industry whether by fiscal measures or by investment means, but he said that no measures were imminent.

Fiat shares had hit a day's low of 4,230 lire after Monday's closing price of 4,378 lire, largely in response to the poor nine-month results issued after the bourse closed on Monday. These nine-month results showed a fall in pretax profits of around 36 percent.
